name: cohere-empty-placeholder
purpose: convertCohereMessages replaces an EMPTY messages array with one user turn carrying PROMPT_PLACEHOLDER (prompt-converters.js:384-390); the text is getConfigValue('promptPlaceholder', "Let's get started.") at :4, and this scenario's config sets no promptPlaceholder, so the pinned DEFAULT is what must appear. DISCRIMINATING BECAUSE: the recorded body's messages must be exactly one user turn whose content is that sentence -- an empty messages array would show the branch did not run, and every other cohere scenario carries probe markers instead, so the two bodies cannot be confused.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.rule: the value is compared as the literal "Bearer <synthetic cohere key>", never as a recorded secret
tier2.reason: the scenario declares the key it plants, so the value is the contract (a wrong secret NAME would send a different or no token)

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: COHERE has NO reverse_proxy and NO custom_url: sendCohereRequest assigns the hardcoded literal API_COHERE_V2 and appends '/chat', so the pinned leg can only reach the recorder through the probe transport redirect and the Go leg through its seam. The PATH is untouched and IS compared, which is the part the pinned literal decides.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
